done_when: A thread follow-up starts a turn only when the new batch has a message from an allowed sender, proven by a test where only the root sender is allowed and another person's follow-up gets no reply

findings.body: The required end-to-end proof is still missing. This test exercises real persistence and admission, but replaces the internal runner with `runAgent` and replaces continuation delivery with an array append (lines 141–145). The fake runner never handles a continuation or produces its reply. Production instead defaults to `spawnAgent` (apps/core/src/app/bootstrap/runtime-app.ts:155). These assertions meaningfully cover forwarding, but do not meet the review requirement to fake only third-party services at their edge. Add a required test through the running runtime and real runner transport, faking the channel/model services at their external boundaries, that proves Bob receives no reply with Alice's runner both stopped and still waiting.
findings.title: Not done: prove thread follow-up sender authorization through the real runtime

why: Anyone can get a reply in a thread an allowed person started, because the thread check never looks at who sent the new message
